verdict: Micron's revenue quintupled in a year to $54.2B — AI data centers are buying every memory chip it can make, at prices so high that 87 cents of each sales dollar survived as gross profit.

segments.name: Core Data Center
segments.note: SSDs and memory for data-center builders — a year ago this was a $1.6B business; AI servers changed that.

segments.name: Cloud Memory
segments.note: HBM — the high-bandwidth memory stacked onto AI chips — plus memory for the giant cloud companies; an 83% gross margin business.

segments.name: Mobile and Client
segments.note: Memory and storage for phones and PCs — device makers are paying shortage prices to secure supply.

segments.name: Automotive and Embedded
segments.note: Chips for cars, factories and connected gadgets.

segments.name: All other
segments.note: Small leftovers outside the four business units.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Designing denser, faster memory — a smaller slice of revenue than ever, because sales exploded.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Selling chips and running the company.

opex.name: Other operating expense
opex.note: Mostly a $500M patent-license charge (see one-time items) — not part of making or selling memory.

takeaways.title: The memory supercycle
takeaways.text: Revenue went from $11.3B to $54.2B in a year. Full-year revenue was $133B — three and a half times the year before.

takeaways.title: Scarcity pricing
takeaways.text: Gross margin hit 87%, up from 45% a year ago: when every chip is spoken for before it is made, the maker sets the price.

takeaways.title: Next quarter: bigger
takeaways.text: Micron guided the current quarter to about $61.5B of revenue — it expects the shortage, and the pricing power, to continue.

oneTimers: A $500M patent-license charge sits inside 'other operating expense' — a one-off legal cost of the quarter, unrelated to selling memory. Excluding such items, non-GAAP net income was $38.4B ($33.42 a share) versus $37.7B GAAP.
otherDetail: Interest income of $575M on Micron's growing cash pile plus $46M from equity investments, less $88M of other non-operating costs — a net +$533M.
follow100Note: Other income adds $0.98 per $100 of revenue; the rows reconcile to $100 at this rounding.
footerNote: Business-unit revenues are as reported by Micron; 'All other' is the small residual outside the four units.
